en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan from Muhammad b. al-Hassan al-Saffar from al-Hassan b. Musa al-Khashab from Abdillah b. Jabalah from Ghiyath b. Kalub from Ishaq b. Ammar who said:
I asked Abi Abdillah (a.s.): "Oh Aba Abdillah, inform me about the best times during the Fajr prayer."
He replied: "It is at the time of the dawn.
Verily, Allah, the Most High, says, 'Indeed, the recitation of the Qur'an at dawn is ever witnessed.' [17:78].
Meaning, it is witnessed by the angels of the day and the angels of the night.
So when the servant prays Salaat al-Subh at the start of dawn, its reward would be noted down twice, noted by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.”
